newsitem.title: USA: SOCCER-MCBRIDE GOAL LIFTS EAST TO MLS ALL-STAR VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MCBRIDE GOAL LIFTS EAST TO MLS ALL-STAR VICTORY.

text.p: Columbus Crew forward Brian McBride scored with two minutes remaining in regulation to lift the Eastern Conference to a 5-4 victory over the Western Conference in the second Major League Soccer All-Star Game on Wednesday night.
Tampa Bay Mutiny and Colombian midfielder Carlos Valderrama, who scored one goal and set up two others, was voted Most Valuable Player for the second consecutive year in the All-Star Game.
"I enjoyed both games," Valderrama said. "But I enjoyed this one more because we scored more goals."
The game, played before a rain-drenched crowd of 24,816 at Giants Stadium, featured nine goals, heroics from several players and comebacks from each team.
"It was everything you wanted to see except solid defence," said Kansas City Wizards and West coach Ron Newman. "Maybe it will catch on if we play more games like that."

The West grabbed a 2-0 halftime lead before the East rallied for a 4-2 advantage. The West, however, struck twice in six minutes to force a 4-4 tie before McBride tucked a 12-yard shot under Mexican goalkeeper Jorge Campos of the Los Angeles Galaxy.

The West struck first on a goal by Dallas Burn forward Dante Washington in the 11th minute. Washington, a reserve put into the starting lineup after San Jose striker Eric Wynalda could not play due to groin surgery, knocked in a Preki cross from the right wing from four yards (metres) past goalkeeper Walter Zenga of Italy.

Campos, who replaced Swiss midfielder Alain Sutter of the Dallas Burn in the 34th minute, made it 2-0 with a brilliant goal in the 43rd minute. Campos raced down the right side past defender Jeff Agoos and fired a four yard (metres) shot from a severe angle to the near post that bounded off the crossbar and into the net. It was Campos's first MLS goal.
The East took over for most of the second half.
Valderrama scored off a 14-yard in the 50th minute and Tampa teammate Giuseppe Galderisi of Italy converted a 3-on-1 break off a Valderrama pass in the 63rd minute.

Columbus Crew midfielder Robert Warzycha of Poland gave the East a 3-2 lead with an eight-yard shot in the 66th minute and D.C. United forward Richie Williams made it a two-goal bulge four minutes later.

After a 10-minute scoring silence, the West broke through in the 80th minute as Kansas City and Zimbabwean international forward Digital Takawira beat New York/New Jersey MetroStars goalkeeper Tony Meola with a six yard (metres) header in the 80th minute and Los Angeles and U.S. international midfielder Cobi Jones tied it, putting in a rebound of a shot by Scotland's Mo Johnston in the 86th minute.
That set up McBride's late heroics. McBride tucked a pass from Galderisi under Campos from 12 yards (metres).
"The way the game was going, it could have been anybody," McBride said. "This type of game is so much fun for a forward, hell for a defender."

Eastern Conference: Walter Zenga (Tony Meola, 45th); Jeff Agoos, Alexi Lalas (Ted Chronopoulos, 45th), Eddie Pope (Frank Yallop, 45th); John Harkes (Richie Williams, 45th), Roberto Donadoni (Steve Ralston, 28th); Carlos Valderrama, Robert Warzycha; Mlkq9HQ:cheverry (Chinquinho Conde, 45th); Jaime Moreno (Brian McBride, 45th), Raul Diaz Arce (Giuseppe Galderisi, 45th).

Western Conference: Mark Dodd; Richard Gough (John Doyle, 45th), Marcelo Balboa (Mo Johnston, 45th), Diego Sonora; Chris Henderson, Mauricio Cienfuegos, Alain Sutter (Jorge Campos, 34th), Preki (Mark Santel, 45th); Dante Washington; Vitalis Takawira (Ronald Cerritos, 45th), Damian (Cobi Jones, 45th).
